shortlist.name: FLOWBACK-S (merge: FLOWBACK + SPRINT, ECHO-small-print folded in as feature)
shortlist.verdict: test-first — the strongest breadth-x-horizon route to Sharpe; the two proposals are the same trade and the merge keeps the best defenses of each (quiet-sibling news control, explicit spread-cost gate, profit-target exit). Main survival question is purely empirical: does the rebound net of the ask clear ~0.5pt.
shortlist.refined_spec: Universe: gate >=8 print days in trailing 90 AND >=15 active days in trailing 90 (kills the trivial-4x problem on sparse bonds); mat 1-7y; cs 0.8-5%; mid_t >= 70; trailing-60d median observed (s_px - p_px) <= 1.0 pt on >=5 paired days. Signal day t requires ALL: (1) qvolume_t >= 4x trailing-90d median daily qvolume AND >= $1mm par; (2) mid_t <= trailing-15d median mid (>=4 print days) - 1.25 pts; (3) sibling news check: among gated same-issuer (6-char) bonds printing in [t-5,t], none down >0.5 pt vs its own 15d median -> full size; no sibling printed -> half size; any sibling down >0.5 pt -> veto. Optional confirmation feature (from ECHO): sibling marked down on <= $500k 5-day volume upgrades conviction, never gates. Entry: first ask strictly after t within 7d, filled only if ask <= mid_t + 0.25 — THE SAME FILL CAP MUST BE APPLIED TO THE MATCHED CONTROL or excess is inflated. Exit: first bid >= entry+5d once latest mid >= frozen pre-event 15d median - 0.25, OR first bid >= entry+1.5 pts profit target, whichever first; time stop first bid after entry+35d; stale = last bid <= entry+60d. Sizing: proportional to concession depth, cap 2x unit, 1 position/issuer, <=1% NAV. IS discipline: one monotonicity sweep over (volume multiple, drop size, window), freeze one operating point before OOS.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Highest expected honest Sharpe contribution: thousands of scattered idiosyncratic events/yr, ~15d holds (1/5 the vol of GRANITE holds), and the only fast spec whose cost hurdle is engineered explicitly (spread gate <= 1.0 pt vs 1.25+ pt expected reversion). Also the cheapest to falsify: if the post-fill rebound is < 0.5pt net, kill it in week one of IS testing and the whole fast tier reprices.

shortlist.name: COILSPRING (mild-widening spread reversion, GRANITE complement)
shortlist.verdict: test-first — direct extension of the repo's only proven edge (short-dated crossover reversion, OOS +3.5%) to the 5-10x more frequent sub-3pt dislocations GRANITE cannot see; the explicit GRANITE carve-out makes additivity mechanical, not hoped-for.
shortlist.refined_spec: As proposed with one added artifact killer: the widening must persist on >=2 distinct print days in [t-3,t] (one bid-side print cannot trigger). Universe: gate; mat 1-5; entry cs 1.5-5%; mid <= 102; >=8 cs prints in trailing 60d. Entry when: cs_t >= m60 (shift-1 trailing-60d median cs) + max(0.0075, 0.004 + 0.004/mat); NOT a GRANITE trigger (mid > 60d median mid - 3); cs/mat above cross-sectional median of eligible set; cs <= 5% on the widened print. First ask <= 7d. Size ~ widening depth, cap 2x. Exit: min hold 21d, first bid once cs <= m60(recomputed) + 25bp, or mat < 0.75, or 240d stop. IS decision gate (pre-registered): excess-vs-control must be positive AND monotone in widening size above the noise floor; flat = sleeve dead, no re-tuning.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Second because it inherits the most validated priors in the repo (zone, direction, pull-to-par mechanism) and has the largest breadth of any spec — but its killer risk (75bp 'widening' on 1-2y bonds = one bid-side print, order of the bid/ask itself) is exactly what the matched control adjudicates, so it must be tested early with the persistence filter on/off reported.

shortlist.name: TWINS-R (merge: TWINS + SISTERS + LADDERGAP + both LADDERs; change-based only, level-based rotation killed)
shortlist.verdict: test-first — five near-duplicate drafts collapse to one sleeve. The level-based variants (cheapest-to-own-curve rotation) are rejected: with no seniority/callability fields, 'cheap to curve' is structurally confounded and the excess would be tranche risk premium, not timing. Only the fresh-divergence (change) version isolates timing alpha.
shortlist.refined_spec: Universe: issuer (6-char) with >=3 gated bonds; bond mat 1-7; entry cs 1-6%; mid >= 70; gate on bond and counted siblings. Sibling set: same issuer, |mat_j - mat_i| <= 2, print within 10d, count >= 2. gap_t = cs_i - median sibling cs. Entry requires ALL: (a) gap_t - trailing-60d median gap (shift-1, >=20 obs) >= 75bp; (b) z-score >= 2.0; (c) persistence: condition (a) held at >=50bp on >=3 distinct print days in [t-10,t] (kills one-print artifacts); (d) issuer-quiet certified on FRESH prints only: most-active sibling's cs widened <= 50bp over [t-20,t]; (e) bond itself printed on t. First ask <= 7d; 1 position/issuer. Exit: min hold 10d, first bid once gap - frozen entry median <= 25bp; hard stop 180d; abandon if sibling structure breaks 30d. Report the fraction of entries where the first post-signal ask already snapped back (signal-to-fill decay) — the proposers' own top failure mode.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Third because it is the portfolio's diversification engine: issuer-differenced P&L is the only stream in the dataset structurally orthogonal to both credit beta and the 2021-23 rates regime, so even at standalone Sharpe ~1 it buys more book-level Sharpe than a correlated Sharpe-1.5 sleeve. Test after the two reversal sleeves because its per-trade margin is thinnest (~1pt convergence vs 0.6-1.2pt round trip) and its verdict depends on fill quality data the first two tests will already have produced.

shortlist.name: CREST (issuer-level 6-1 spread-tightening momentum)
shortlist.verdict: test-first — the only WINNERS strategy in the pool, hence the cheapest correlation hedge to a book that is otherwise all losers/reversion; documented anomaly (NIG momentum), spread-space ranking strips the rates contamination, and ~1x annual turnover via hysteresis genuinely clears the cost hurdle.
shortlist.refined_spec: As proposed: month-end t, universe = gated bonds, mat 2-10, cs_1m 1.5-5%. Issuer signal S = median cs[t-42,t-21) - median cs[t-168,t-126), >=3 prints per sub-window (6-1 skip-month, issuer-median construction kills bounce and stale-mark momentum). Buy top-quintile tighteners not held, shortest qualifying bond with mat >= 2, first ask <= 7d. Exit: sell only after S-rank < 50th pct two consecutive month-ends (hysteresis), or cs_1m > 6%, or mat < 1.5, or age > 540d. MANDATORY IS gate before OOS: excess must be monotone across quintiles; if the top quintile is not distinguishably better than Q2-Q3, freeze at reject. Note the acknowledged conservative bias: tighteners have below-average forward carry, so the control comparison understates this sleeve — disclose, do not adjust.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Fourth: expected standalone excess is modest (residual continuation after paying the ask into 6-month winners may be 1-2%/yr), but its monthly-mark correlation to the reversal sleeves should be low-to-negative, and momentum-crash months (2009Q2, Apr-2020) are precisely when the reversal sleeves feast — the interleaving is the value. Cheap to implement (monthly, issuer-level) and the quintile monotonicity test is a fast kill switch.

shortlist.name: BALLAST-K (merge: BALLAST + LADDER-X; short-crossover carry ladder with knife veto)
shortlist.verdict: test-first — but judged honestly as the CAGR/base layer, not as timing alpha: the control comparison will and should show small excess (the veto is the only timing content, likely +0.5-1%/yr). It exists so the book can reach 10% CAGR while the event sleeves supply the Sharpe. LADDER-X's momentum gate adds nothing the veto doesn't; its hold-to-maturity exit-spread compression is kept.
shortlist.refined_spec: Month-end t: rank gated bonds with mat 1-4, cs 1.5-5%, mid 85-100.5, trailing-90d qvolume >= $1mm, ytw >= T-bill + 2%, KNIFE VETO: mid(t) >= 60d-reference mid - 2.0 AND >= 20d-reference mid - 1.0. Buy top 60 by cs not held, first ask <= 7d, equal units, issuer cap 2. Exit: hold to mat < 0.5 then first bid (near-par exit compresses the second spread leg, per LADDER-X), or cs < 0.8% (rich), or 720d stop. Momentum-stop decision PRE-REGISTERED: measure the stop's IS contribution once; if negative (the 2022 failure mode — selling rates-driven marks at wide bids), ship entry-veto-only, frozen. Percentile-vs-absolute cs band decided once on IS, frozen. Report Sharpe with stale-mark fraction and with the volume floor doubled as sensitivity — this sleeve is the most stale-mark-flattered of the book.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Fifth: near-certain to 'work' in absolute terms (front-end HY carry), so the test is not survival but calibration — quantifying the veto's excess, the stale-mark haircut, and the sleeve's crisis correlation to the reversal sleeves, all inputs the architecture needs before weights can be set. No point testing the portfolio layer before this base layer's true vol is known.

shortlist.name: DEBUT (new-issue concession with sibling-relative gate)
shortlist.verdict: test-first — the one venue where a short-horizon cash-bond trade faces its lifetime-minimum bid/ask, with thousands of events/yr and an honest sibling-relative cheapness gate; but the debut-identification artifact (re-CUSIPs, TRACE dissemination phase-ins) must be quarantined before any number is believed.
shortlist.refined_spec: As proposed, plus mandatory artifact quarantine: parameter calibration uses only debuts after 2007-01, and the 2014-07..2015-06 wave (144A dissemination onset) is excluded from ALL calibration (kept in reporting, flagged). Event: first-ever print t0 (t0 >= sample_start + 200d), debut mid in [97,103], mat >= 2, >=3 print days in [t0,t0+5], >= $25mm cumulative volume. Concession gate on t in [t0+3, t0+15]: ytw >= maturity-matched (|dmat| <= 2) gated-sibling 30d median ytw + 20bp; no sibling, no trade. First ask <= 7d after t. Exit: first bid in [entry+45, entry+90]; stale = last bid <= entry+120. Control on the same debut universe with random timing inside the debut window — only within-window timing counts as alpha. Report IS-era vs OOS-era decay explicitly (index funds now buy debuts; decay is the expected failure).
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Sixth: genuinely uncorrelated event stream (supply-driven, fires in calm markets when reversal sleeves are idle) and the best cost geometry in the dataset, but two real risks — concession consumed pre-secondary, and post-2016 anomaly decay — mean expected OOS contribution is moderate. Test needs the debut-artifact audit first, which is standalone work.

shortlist.name: ENDGAME (index-exclusion pull-to-par at the mat 2->1 flip)
shortlist.verdict: test-first — the vol-suppressor: sub-1y money-good paper with terminal value pinned at par is the cheapest monthly-mark stabilizer available, and the calendar-forced-seller mechanism is real. Economically thin per trade; lives or dies on the spread-cost gate.
shortlist.refined_spec: As proposed, with two hardenings: (1) the mat-flip-to-exclusion offset is calibrated ONCE on IS (locate the post-flip cheapening peak) and frozen — it is the spec's one legitimate free parameter; (2) added cost gate: skip any bond whose trailing-60d median (s_px - p_px) > 0.5 pt — a 40bp yield concession (~0.3pt price) cannot clear a wider toll. Event: first in-panel flip mat 2->1; baseline B = median (ytw - tbill3m) over [t1-120, t1-10] (>=8 prints). Signal: any t in [t1, t1+60] with (ytw - tbill3m) >= B + 0.40. Money-good gates: mid >= 92, cs <= 3.5%, ytw <= 8, no mid < 80 in trailing 250d. First ask <= 7d, one entry/bond. Exit: first bid after entry+30 once trailing-5d (ytw - tbill3m) <= B, else first bid in [entry+150, entry+240]; stale <= entry+270; never hold to final print. Report Sharpe with stale-mark haircut (this sleeve is maximally exposed) and the loser tail explicitly (short paper gapping to 60 is the negative-skew profile).
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Seventh: expected excess CAGR is small (2-4%) so it cannot carry the book, but if the concession clears the 0.5pt cost gate its near-zero mark vol raises book-level Sharpe disproportionately. Test after the main sleeves because its portfolio value depends on how much vol the rest of the book actually has.

shortlist.name: ANGELFALL-M (merge: ANGELFALL + ANGELFLOW; fallen-angel proxy, idiosyncratic crossings)
shortlist.verdict: test-first (last slot) — best-documented anomaly in the pool, but the weakest proxy: without ratings the cs-migration trigger may fire 2-6 weeks after the rating event, i.e. after the reversion, leaving beta-with-lag. ANGELFALL's version wins the merge (exhaustion-timed entry, idiosyncratic cap); ANGELFLOW is retired.
shortlist.refined_spec: As ANGELFALL proposed: event e when trailing-20d median cs first exceeds 3.0% with 90d-median (as of e-60) <= 2.0%; forced-flow confirmation: [e-5,e+15] volume >= 4x prior 21d average AND mid >= 4pts below [e-60,e-10] median; idiosyncratic cap: < 1.5% of gated universe simultaneously crossing (point-in-time). Entry t in [e+10, e+40] when trailing-5d volume < 1.5x pre-event average AND cs <= 5.5% AND mid >= 70; first ask <= 7d. Universe mat 2-10, gate, 1-yr cooldown/bond. Exit: first bid in [entry+120, entry+240], early from +45 if 10d median cs <= 3.0%; stale <= entry+300. MANDATORY reporting: (a) with AND without the 1.5% crossing cap — the cap is a cousin of the rejected regime gate and must not silently carry the result; (b) month-clustered bootstrap for the Sharpe CI (events arrive in waves; trade count overstates independence); (c) control shares the FULL filter chain.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Eighth: high per-trade expectation but low, clustered event count and the largest proxy-timing risk in the pool — its plausible best case is a modest, lumpy sleeve capped at ~1/3 book vol. Worth one honest test because the mechanism is the literature's strongest; not worth designing the book around.

shortlist.name: CROSSED-X (merge: CROSSED + CROSSFIRE; crossed-market / cross-sided dominance probe)
shortlist.verdict: test-later — both specs select on extremity of a size-mixed daily VWAP observation, i.e. partially on measurement noise, with odd-lot capacity risk and a fat adverse-selection tail (an ask below recent bids is often the first print at a new lower fair value). The honest next-ask fill is a real defense, so it earns a cheap probe — after the top-8 verdicts arrive.
shortlist.refined_spec: Single merged probe, CROSSED chassis with CROSSFIRE's flow-reality floor and its own level-control: signal t when s_px_t <= trailing-20d median p_px (>=4 bid prints) - 0.25, AND signal-day qvolume >= $250k, AND level-unchanged control: mid_t within 1.5 pts of trailing-20d median mid (proves the ask is dislocated, not the market trending down). Universe: gate tightened to >=12 prints/90d; mat 1-6; cs <= 5%; mid >= 75; trailing-60d median spread <= 1.5 pts. Entry: first ask <= 7d filled only if ask <= frozen L (limit semantics — identical cap on the control). Exit: first bid >= entry+3d at entry ask + 0.50 target, else first bid after entry+25d; stale <= entry+45d. Report: fill rate, signal-to-fill slippage, and left-tail (continuation) frequency — if >40% of fills continue down 2+ pts, kill.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Test-later: expected surviving breadth after the level-unchanged filter is a few hundred events/yr — too thin to be a pillar, and its data-artifact risk means an IS pass is weak evidence. Run it once the FLOWBACK-S infrastructure exists (shares 90% of the code) as a marginal-cost experiment.

shortlist.name: WALLBREAK (refi-resolution sibling lag)
shortlist.verdict: test-later — plausible, genuinely novel mechanism (front bond as refi-probability gauge) with a structurally truncated left tail, but a few hundred IS events against ~6 hand-set parameters cannot produce a defensible significance claim; and TRACE-era dealers may arbitrage the issuer curve same-day, leaving no lag.
shortlist.refined_spec: Pre-register EXACTLY as proposed (front bond: mid <= 96 and 20d cs >= 3% at some point in [e-120,e-10]; resolution: 5d median mid >= 99; sibling: mat 2-8, cs 2-6%, mid >= 75, cs >= 80% of its 60d max; entry [e, e+15] first ask <= 7d; exit first bid [entry+90, entry+210], early at cs <= 60% of entry 60d-max; max 2 siblings/issuer/event, 1-yr cooldown) with ZERO parameter iteration — the parameters are frozen now, before any backtest, because with N in the hundreds any tuning is pure overfit. Report the point estimate with month-clustered CI and the fraction of events where siblings had already repriced before entry (the no-lag failure diagnostic). Ship only if the CI excludes zero; otherwise archive as an opportunistic overlay.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Test-later purely on statistical power: even a true edge cannot be demonstrated at this N without the pre-registration discipline above, and the desk's test budget is better spent where breadth allows a verdict.

shortlist.name: EBB (cohort-relative laggard catch-up)
shortlist.verdict: test-later — the spec most exposed to the stale-quote illusion (a laggard's flat mid is often just an unrefreshed mark that 'catches up' at exactly the print where you'd be filled), and its cohort-rallied >= +1pt gate is a market-state condition of the same class as the regime gate the repo already rejected OOS. The proposer's own best case is 'small diversifier'.
shortlist.refined_spec: If tested: as proposed (cohorts = cs {1-2%, 2-4%} x mat {1-3, 3-6}; rel3 = 3M return minus cohort median; buy bottom quintile subject to own-1M >= -1pt, not-GRANITE-dislocated, >=6 prints in trailing 30d) but with the cohort-rally gate REMOVED as the primary spec and included only as a reported IS variant — if the edge exists solely with the gate on, that is the regime-gate signature and the sleeve is rejected. Exit: monthly, sell when rel3 >= cohort median, or 6 month-ends, or cs_1m > 5%, or gate failure 2 consecutive month-ends. The honest ask-entry engine is the arbiter: a surviving edge here is highly credible, a null is expected.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Test-later: expected excess is the smallest of the survivors (proposer concedes a realistic -0.5%/yr bleed scenario), but the test is nearly free once the monthly cross-sectional infrastructure exists for CREST, and a surviving result would be unusually trustworthy given the engine kills the phantom-mark artifact. Marginal-cost science, not a pillar.

shortlist.name: SLIDE (rolldown rider with tier-matched steepness gate)
shortlist.verdict: reject — adverse selection by construction: tiers are formed on cs and then the 'cheap half of the cell' is selected on the same variable, so cheap-for-tier structurally means migrating-to-next-tier, and the yield-backup timing condition preferentially buys names under pressure; duration ~3.5-4 plants it in the documented 2021-23 soft regime where the repo shows no timing edge exists; the trailing-mark vol target reacts a quarter late by design. The proposer's own expected-failure paragraph concedes the acid test fails. Expected honest excess: zero to negative.
shortlist.refined_spec: Not to be implemented. The salvageable ideas are already housed elsewhere: front-end carry+roll lives in BALLAST-K at mat 1-4 (where pull-to-par truncates the migration loss the 4-6y version eats), and the yield-backup entry idea is COILSPRING with a proper reversion target instead of an open-ended ride.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Rejected, not queued: unlike the test-later specs, its identified flaw is structural (selection on the ranking variable), not empirical, so no backtest outcome could rehabilitate the spec as written.

shortlist.name: ECHO issuer-rv (bellwether lead-lag laggard catch-up)
shortlist.verdict: reject — episodic by the proposer's own analysis: the edge concentrates in 8-10 crisis-recovery windows over 23 years, which cannot support a monthly Sharpe-3 statistic regardless of per-episode quality; between episodes the rule fires on stale-quote mirages ('unchanged' laggard cs = old print whose first real ask already embeds the catch-up) and pays the spread for nothing, dragging excess toward zero. Also duplicates TWINS-R's issuer machinery while inverting its (stronger) news-control logic.
shortlist.refined_spec: Not to be implemented as a sleeve. One element is worth carrying: the co-mover requirement (bonds within 30bp of each other at some point in [t-90,t-30]) is a good structural-comparability filter and is available as an optional tightening of TWINS-R's sibling set if IS shows structural-cheapness contamination there.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Rejected: an episodic strategy competes for capital with GRANITE itself (which already owns the crisis-recovery trade with 96% win in 2020) and adds no independent monthly observations — the scarce resource a Sharpe target needs.

shortlist.name: ECHO microstructure (small-print sympathy markdown)
shortlist.verdict: reject as standalone, folded into FLOWBACK-S — four conjunctive filters plus a tight fill cap starve the sample (proposer estimates possibly double-digit events/yr), and the fills that survive skew toward genuine issuer deterioration (news is precisely when retail dumps small lots while dealers still lift offers). The proposer pre-authorized this fold-back and the synthesis takes it.
shortlist.refined_spec: Implemented only as the optional confirmation feature inside FLOWBACK-S: when the traded (loud) bond's signal coincides with a sibling marked down on <= $500k of 5-day volume, conviction sizing may increase within the existing 2x cap. No separate positions, no separate parameters.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Rejected as a sleeve on sample-size arithmetic alone; its information content survives at zero marginal cost as a FLOWBACK-S sizing input, which is the correct altitude for a signal this thin.

shortlist.name: MOSAIC/GYROSCOPE (merged portfolio layer)
shortlist.verdict: test-later — not a sleeve but the combination layer; merged into one architecture (below) and tested ONLY after per-sleeve IS verdicts exist. MOSAIC's LQD duration throttle is killed now: it is a market-regime gate of exactly the class the repo rejected on OOS evidence (IS +4.21% -> OOS +0.94%); duration is controlled structurally by maturity caps instead. GYROSCOPE's no-forced-early-exit principle and MOSAIC's per-sleeve control mandate are both kept.
shortlist.refined_spec: See portfolio_architecture. Key merged rules: inverse-vol sleeve weights on trailing 24 monthly marks (12-month floor, fixed priors before that; the RULE, not fitted weights, carries to OOS); book vol target 5% ann via scale = min(1, 0.05/sigma_book), no leverage, residual in 3M T-bills; caps 0.5% NAV/CUSIP, 2%/issuer across all sleeves; de-gross by attrition only — the portfolio layer never forces a sale (a forced sale pays the bid and injects hidden timing into the control comparison); NO duration throttle, NO portfolio stop-loss; per-sleeve matched controls mandatory (a dead sleeve must not hide inside a live book); stale-mark fraction reported at book and sleeve level.
shortlist.test_order_rationale: Sequenced last by dependency, not by merit: every input it needs (sleeve vols, correlations incl. crisis-month subset, stale-mark haircuts) is an output of the sleeve tests. Its one falsifiable claim — pairwise monthly-mark correlations <= ~0.4 — is the book's single biggest risk and gets measured on IS with a crisis-months-only sub-matrix before any OOS run.

portfolio_architecture:
Three-tier long-only book, GRANITE excluded everywhere (every sleeve carries an explicit not-a-GRANITE-trigger carve-out or a disjoint event definition), combined by a single frozen rule set (merged MOSAIC/GYROSCOPE, duration throttle deleted).

TIER 1 — BASE / CAGR ENGINE (~40% of risk budget): BALLAST-K (short-crossover carry ladder, knife veto) plus ENDGAME (sub-1y exclusion harvest) as the mark-vol suppressor. These supply accrual and pin the denominator; their measured timing excess is expected small and they are sold internally as diversifiers, never as alpha headlines.

TIER 2 — FAST IDIOSYNCRATIC / SHARPE ENGINE (~35%): FLOWBACK-S, COILSPRING, TWINS-R. Overlap resolution is mechanical and pre-committed: where FLOWBACK-S and COILSPRING both fire on a bond, FLOWBACK-S takes the trade (the volume-confirmed event is the stronger identification); TWINS-R is capped at 1 position/issuer and the cross-sleeve issuer cap (2% NAV) binds all three. These three carry the burden of proof for the Sharpe-3 target: if FLOWBACK-S and TWINS-R do not clear the spread on IS, the honest target resets to Sharpe ~2.

TIER 3 — SLOW / ORTHOGONAL (~25%): CREST (winners-momentum — the anti-correlated stream to a reversion-heavy book), DEBUT (supply-cycle events, fires in calm markets), ANGELFALL-M (episodic, hard-capped at 1/3 of the tier).

COMBINATION RULES (all frozen before OOS): monthly inverse-vol sleeve weighting on trailing 24 monthly marks (12-month floor; fixed tier priors 40/35/25 before histories exist; the rule travels to OOS, never the fitted weights); book-level vol target 5% annualized, scale = min(1, 0.05/sigma_book), hard no-leverage cap, residual in 3M T-bills (real carry 2023+); concentration caps 0.5% NAV per CUSIP and 2% per issuer enforced at fill time across all sleeves; de-grossing by attrition only — the portfolio layer never forces an exit (forced sales pay the bid and contaminate the per-sleeve control comparison); no portfolio stop-loss and no market-state throttle (both are the regime-gate class the repo rejected on OOS evidence).

VALIDATION PROTOCOL: (1) each sleeve tested against its own matched random-entry control sharing the FULL filter chain including any conditional fill caps — fill caps applied asymmetrically are the single most likely way this book fakes alpha; (2) IS correlation matrix reported twice — all months, and crisis months only (2008H2, Mar-2020, 2022H1) — because the dominant book risk is correlation convergence among sleeves that are all long short-dated crossover credit; (3) Sharpe reported raw and with a stale-mark haircut (stale fraction disclosed per sleeve; BALLAST-K and ENDGAME are the most flattered); (4) month-clustered bootstrap for all CIs (ANGELFALL-M and WALLBREAK events cluster); (5) one IS parameter sweep per sleeve with monotonicity requirement, then total freeze; the one-shot OOS 2016-2025 run is final, no post-OOS iteration.

HONEST EXPECTATION: sleeves individually at monthly-mark Sharpe ~0.8-1.5; at realistic pairwise rho 0.3-0.5 the combined risk-asset stream lands ~1.8-2.5, plus T-bill carry on ~20-30% average cash at the 5% vol target. Sharpe 3 / 10% CAGR is reachable only in the branch where FLOWBACK-S and TWINS-R both clear costs decisively AND correlations hold near 0.3; the architecture is built so that the fallback (Tier 1 + CREST + whatever fast sleeves survive) is still a shippable Sharpe ~1.5-2, CAGR ~7-8% book rather than a failure.
